label: input token l in the original phase (positions 2-6)
explanation: Token detector for the letter l during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. Essentially all activation mass (>99.9%) is on steps where the input is l; it fires on about 87% of l inputs at t>=2. Very weak at t=1 (rate 0.2%) and absent at t=0. It fades by t=7 and is absent at t>=8, which is why the window is restricted to 2-6. Mean mass peaks for l at t=3-4. A repeated l (not its first occurrence) gives smaller activations; the top activations are a first l at t=4 in sequences that start with e/b. It never fires on the delimiter and almost never in the copy phase, even when l is fed back as a copied input or is the token being output. It does not fire on other tokens.

issues: I could reproduce the test-split scores: P 0.955, R 0.962, F1 0.958, mass recall 0.991.
The '87% of l at t>=2' claim checks out: the predicate in_tok==l & phase 0 & t>=2 has precision 0.865 on test.
The copy-phase claim checks out. In dev there are 18 active steps out of 2.7M. The predicates phase 2 & in_tok==l and phase 2 & out_tok==l both get F1 0.0. The feature never fires on the delimiter.
The first-occurrence claim checks out. Adding in_first==1 gives test F1 0.920, worse than 0.958. Repeated l at t=2-6 still fires 93% of the time, with less mass.

The t=1 and t=7 claims check out. At t=1 the firing rate on l is 6.5% (mass 0.2%). At t=7 it is 23% (mass 0.7%). At t>=8 there are 25 activations in dev. These are faint edge effects, not a missed class.

The false-positive claim checks out. Of about 2,990 test false positives, roughly 1,860 are l at t=6 (precision 0.775) and roughly 880 are l at t=2 (precision 0.947). Neither depends on L: at t=6, L=7 and L>=8 give about the same precision (0.78 and 0.77). The rendered misses look like scattered positional decay, not a token or history pattern.

Minor: the claim that the top activations are a first l at t=4 in sequences starting with e or b comes only from the top examples and was not scored. The explanation says so itself, so this is not an overclaim.
